headline: Risk appetite cools as Fed hawkishness and Mideast tensions bite
body: Futures opened September on the defensive, with Dow contracts off roughly half a percent and Nasdaq-100 futures down closer to a full point, as renewed Iran-linked shipping attacks near the Strait of Hormuz dimmed hopes for a quick reopening and pushed Brent back toward the high-eighties. That's compounding pressure from the rates side: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's recent remarks that inflation isn't meaningfully cooling have pushed market-implied odds of a September rate hike to roughly 57%, up sharply from about 40% a week earlier, while the 10-year Treasury yield has climbed toward 4.75% after three straight up sessions. The S&P 500 remains close to record territory, but the combination of sticky-inflation rhetoric and a real geopolitical risk premium in energy has visibly softened the momentum built up over a strong summer.

Retail chatter today leans more on individual names than on a broad directional call: Nvidia, Alphabet and Micron are drawing bullish mention volume alongside post-earnings strength in Salesforce, CrowdStrike and Okta, while GameStop and Nike are seeing outsized jumps in mentions without an obvious fundamental trigger. The other side of higher-for-longer rate expectations is showing up in small caps, which are lagging as rate-sensitive names absorb the yield move. Taken together, the setup reads less like broad-based fear and more like a rotation toward earnings-validated large caps and away from anything exposed to rates or oil — a cautious, stock-picker's tone rather than a wholesale risk-off retreat.
